subject.title: Feat: Add Trivy SBOM and vulnerability scanning to Docker release

question: Should the Docker release workflow start uploading Trivy SARIF/SBOM artifacts and failing releases on fixed CRITICAL findings before this PR has live tag/backfill proof?
rationale: This changes production release automation and adds an external scanner, Code Scanning upload path, artifact path, and release-failing gate that static checks cannot prove end to end.

options.title: Require live release proof
options.body: Ask for a redacted tag/backfill or equivalent workflow run showing Trivy install, scans, SARIF uploads, artifact upload, and the critical gate before merge.

options.title: Merge with owner-accepted risk
options.body: A release/security owner can intentionally accept the unproven external workflow dependency and handle any release breakage after merge.

options.title: Start advisory-only
options.body: Keep SARIF and artifacts but remove or defer the release-blocking exit path until maintainers have observed successful release runs.

recommendation.title: Require live release proof
recommendation.body: Ask for a redacted tag/backfill or equivalent workflow run showing Trivy install, scans, SARIF uploads, artifact upload, and the critical gate before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Docker release workflow and release-control history makes this the strongest individual routing signal for the release gate choice.
